findings.title: Read check compares MD5 even when the storage returns none, so reads fail on non-GCS files that carry an md5
findings.body: The new branch runs whenever `file.md5` is set and never checks the current side. On S3, Azure, local and other clients, `info_to_file` never fills `md5`, so the current value is always `""`. Any `File` on those storages with a non-empty `md5` therefore fails with `md5 was X, now ` and the read is rejected as "changed on the source". That file could be one the user built with `File(..., md5=...)`, or a GCS File copied or rebased to another source. The PR says MD5 decides only where both rows have it, and `_by_md5` in the diff code follows that rule, but this check does not. Fix: use the MD5 comparison only when the current object also has an MD5, and fall back to the etag otherwise. For example, fetch the current File once, take `current.md5 if file.md5 and current.md5` for the comparison, and else compare etags as before.
